text.p: ZAGREB, May 15 (Croatia) - Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Talks on Croatia joining the World Trade Organisation start in Geneva.
- Economy Minister Nenad Porges holds talks in Washington with officials of the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency.
- Croats win four out of 30 places assigned for foreigners in military academies across the United States. The four will start their four-year education in the U.S. in 1998.
- Why do banks fear the bill against money laundering which proposes that each time a person brings in more than 75,000 kuna in cash this be recorded and the authorities informed.

- Talks between the Croatian Democratic Union and Croatian Social Liberal Party representatives on the establishment of the Zagreb authorities have run into problems while tackling the issue of power-sharing. No date has been set yet for the fourth round of talks.
- The number of people with jobs is down by 400,000 compared to 1990 with 1,000 being left jobless each month due to bankrupcy and another 2,000 due to lay-offs.
- Four people die in Zagreb due to the heatwave that may last throughout May.
- Lorries are banned from driving through Plitvice national park to help preserve its beauty.
- Officials of the Soros Open Society charged with tax evasion plead not guilty. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
